q: What is the main ingredient of an omelette?
fact: A classic French omelette is cooked quickly and rolled so it stays soft inside.

q: Spaghetti bolognese is named after a city in which country?
fact: In Bologna itself, the traditional meat ragù is usually served with tagliatelle, not spaghetti.

q: What colour is the flesh of a typical ripe kiwi fruit?
fact: Kiwi fruit were once sold under the name Chinese gooseberries.

q: Which drink is made from roasted beans and can be served as an espresso?
fact: Coffee beans are actually the seeds of a small, cherry-like fruit.

q: Chips are usually made by cutting up which vegetable?
fact: Potatoes first came to Europe from South America in the 16th century.

q: Which fruit is dried to make raisins?
fact: Sultanas and currants are dried grapes too, just from different varieties.

q: What is the yellow part of an egg called?
fact: The colour of an egg yolk depends largely on what the hen has been eating.

q: Which country is famous for sushi?
fact: The word sushi refers to the seasoned vinegared rice, not the raw fish.

q: Which vegetable is traditionally carved into a lantern at Halloween?
fact: In Ireland and Scotland, people carved turnips long before pumpkins caught on.

q: Tofu is made from which kind of bean?
fact: Tofu is made by curdling soya milk, a bit like the way cheese is made.

q: According to the saying, which fruit a day keeps the doctor away?
fact: Thousands of different apple varieties are grown around the world.

q: Which drink is made by fermenting grapes?
fact: Sparkling wine can only be called Champagne if it comes from the Champagne region of France.

q: Alongside eggs and milk, what is the main ingredient of Yorkshire pudding batter?
fact: Yorkshire puddings were often served with gravy before the meat, to fill people up.

q: What kind of food is cheddar?
fact: Cheddar takes its name from a village in Somerset, near Cheddar Gorge.

q: Penne, fusilli and farfalle are all types of what?
fact: Farfalle means 'butterflies' in Italian, after its bow-tie shape.

q: Tacos and burritos are classic dishes from which country?
fact: Corn tortillas have been eaten in Mexico for thousands of years.

q: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside?
fact: Botanically, strawberries aren't true berries, but bananas are.

q: Tinned baked beans usually come in a sauce made from what?
fact: The beans in a tin of baked beans are usually haricot beans, also called navy beans.

q: Which hot drink, made from dried leaves, is often served with milk in Britain?
fact: Black, green and white teas all come from the same plant, Camellia sinensis.

q: Which long yellow fruit has a skin you peel before eating?
fact: A single banana is called a finger, and a bunch of them is called a hand.

q: Which fish is most commonly used for British fish and chips?
fact: Haddock is the other big favourite, especially in Scotland and the north of England.

q: Popcorn is made by heating the kernels of which plant?
fact: Popcorn pops because the water inside each kernel turns to steam and bursts it open.

q: Which vegetable is famous for making people cry when they chop it?
fact: Chilling an onion in the fridge before cutting it can help reduce the tears.

q: Along with sugar, what is the main ingredient of meringue?
fact: A pinch of cream of tartar helps whisked egg whites hold their shape.

q: Botanically speaking, is a tomato a fruit or a vegetable?
fact: Tomatoes belong to the same plant family as potatoes and aubergines.

q: Which cheese is traditionally used on a margherita pizza?
fact: Mozzarella is stretched and kneaded in hot water, which gives it its stringy texture.

q: Chocolate is made from which beans?
fact: Cocoa pods grow straight out of the trunk and branches of the cacao tree.

q: Which fruit is most often used to make marmalade?
fact: Bitter Seville oranges are prized for marmalade because they set so well.

q: What is the traditional filling of a Cornish pasty?
fact: Genuine Cornish pasties have protected status and must be prepared in Cornwall.

q: Which meat is traditionally served with mint sauce?
fact: Mint sauce is usually made from chopped mint, vinegar and a little sugar.

q: Cider is traditionally made from which fruit?
fact: Perry is a similar drink made by fermenting pears instead of apples.

q: Which herb is the main ingredient of classic green pesto?
fact: Classic pesto comes from Genoa, in the Liguria region of north-west Italy.

q: Which large fruit has a hard, hairy shell and watery juice inside?
fact: Despite its name, a coconut is botanically a drupe rather than a true nut.

q: Which orange vegetable is said to help you see in the dark?
fact: Early cultivated carrots were often purple or yellow rather than orange.

q: The Victoria sponge cake is named after which British monarch?
fact: The Victoria sponge is also called a Victoria sandwich, as the jam is sandwiched between two cakes.
